1. Exemption allowed, subject to just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ('Cr.P.C') has been filed by the petitioners seeking of quashing of FIR bearing no. 108/2014, registered at Police Station Aman Vihar, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Naresh Kumar Chahar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

5. All the petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr.
Sanjay Padam Jain and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Shipra Singh from Police Station Aman Vihar,
Delhi.

6. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner and respondent no. 2 had been solemnized on 08.02.2011 according to Hindu rites at New Delhi and out of this wedlock, no child was born.

It is stated that due to some temperamental differences and matrimonial differences, the complainant/respondent no. 2 left the company of the petitioner no. 1 and started living separately Since February, 2012.

On the complaint of complainant/respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing no.
108/2014 was registered at Police Station Aman Vihar, Delhi, for the offences punishable under Section 498A/406/34 of IPC against petitioners.

It is further stated that petitioner and respondent Pawan And Ors vs The State And Another on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134627980/
1 no. 2 have resolved their disputes amicably before Delhi Mediation Centre, Rohini District Courts,
Delhi vide Settlement Agreement dated 20.12.2021.

sentences.text: 7 . On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties before Delhi Mediation Centre, Rohini District Courts, Delhi vide Settlement Agreement dated 20.12.2021.
8.

entities.text: Delhi Mediation Centre, Rohini District Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner.

9. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 1,70,000/- in three instalments in the following manner:
a. First instalment of Rs. 50,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of first motion of petition.
b. Second instalment of Rs. 50,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of second motion of petition.
c. Second/final instalment of Rs.70,000/- to be paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of quashing of FIR before Hon'ble High Court at New Delhi.
10.
Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received last and final instalment of Rs. 70,000/- today, i.e., 22.03.2023 and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

11. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

12. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 108/2014, registered at Police Station Aman Vihar, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
13. The present petition stands disposed of.
14. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J MARCH 22, 2023/zp
